status: IMPLEMENTED, INTEGRATED and VERIFIED: atomic native core checkpoint and eligible ready-session recovery; overall mission remains active

authority.original_reference_releases: Same independent character/routing/actor manifests as map-runtime-contract.json; no selector or source-value changes.
authority.database_runtime: PostgreSQL-only disposable lab, no SQL Server process in this verification.

source_behavior.finding: Periodic save when the character is main and not in tournament; BOW has a separate branch.
Copies state for DB persistence, excludes unsupported/locked/special contexts; native scope remains normal fresh characters.
Map peer word is MAKEWORD(server_id, SVRGRP_MAPSVR=4). High byte is server type, not application world.
Close every character with a connection on the departing Map. Native crash cleanup preserves fenced database ownership instead of the legacy bulk current-user clear.
Previously recovered TSaveChar/TSaveCharDataStart/End evidence remains authoritative. Checkpoint receipts are an explicit new application contract, not reconstructed historical tables.

persistence_contract: Record initial core plus revision 0 atomically with loaded-to-ready transition; no checkpoint-less native admission.
One latest receipt per character, bounded by character count and removed by authorized hard deletion via FK; not an append-only history or an economy journal.

Receipt contains exact world/character/user/session/node/process/connection identity, recovery version, monotonic revision, stable SHA256 of explicit ordered core bits, SQL core image, timestamp and outcome.
Periodic save holds existing owner-row/account/session locks; updates core and receipt in one transaction, retaining the active login and leaving logout timestamps unchanged.

Identical revision and fingerprint can confirm a previous commit; conflicting payload, skipped/old revision, wrong generation and core drift are refused. Unknown writes are not automatically replayed.

Final save locks the same account and claim, supersedes earlier checkpoints, stamps logout and releases claim/current-user atomically. Exact prior final receipt can confirm completion without another write.
Checkpoint and final-save faults roll back together; late checkpoints cannot recreate a closed claim or overwrite its final core.
One sequential background sweep bounds queued work; each snapshot has an exact claim. Shutdown stops sweeps and awaits background DB operations plus client/World drain.
A checkpoint failure closes the client for a final save; failed final save retains the existing in-memory failure path and nonzero shutdown result. No blind reconnect or write replay is introduced.
recovery_contract: Replacement process first owns the dedicated advisory lock and replaces the token under the owner-row lock, fencing surviving old workers.
Pre-ready claims retain their existing safe cleanup. Ready claims require contract 1, active receipt, exact account/session/character/node/generation and current core equal to recorded core.
Eligible recovery keeps last committed core, changes receipt outcome to recovered, records observed recovery/UTC logout time and removes old claim/current-user in one transaction.

Transient state after saved_at is lost on crash. The interval defaults to 30 minutes, can be shortened to 100..1800000 ms; scheduler/DB backlog affects actual checkpoint age. This is not a zero-loss guarantee.
Already orphaned, pre-018 no-receipt, externally drifted or inconsistent claims stay blocked. Never manufacture receipts or remove claims to make login succeed.
Recovery audit failure refuses startup and preserves prior owner/claim/receipt transaction state.
World retires in-memory characters on unexpected Map TCP loss, without clearing native current-user rows. Correct source server-type ID makes this sweep apply to the actual Map process.

release.note: Installed Release daemons; mounted Debug integration tests.

sanitizer_preset.vptr_excluded: Existing packaged SOCI RTTI limitation; SIGKILL itself cannot execute process-exit leak detection.

real_faults: SIGKILL during a delayed actual PostgreSQL checkpoint: previous committed core/receipt survive; replacement relogin succeeds through the same World.
SIGTERM during ready commit: no stranded account.
SIGTERM during periodic checkpoint: checkpoint and final-save work drain with final position retained.
Control PostgreSQL connection loss: daemon stops with exit 2.
Injected receipt/audit failures: atomic rollback; failed recovery preserves claims.
Concurrent checkpoint/final save: final state wins.
Actual low-level character deletion removes its completed receipt using the Login role.
verification.test_data: Synthetic accounts and explicit fault triggers; original backup-derived reference values unchanged.
verification.client: Independent source-derived encrypted Python peer. Original executable not run.

release.scope: Installed Release Login/World/Map tested. Native integration executables are mounted Debug builds. No original client execution.

remaining: World-link interruption while Map stays alive still needs explicit client drain/rebind behavior; the existing world client reconnect loop alone does not rebuild character registration. Address before secondary transfers.
Secondary Map connections, map/channel transfer claims, full composite synchronization and failure recovery.
Atomic native inventory/equipment/economy/reward operations and their own recovery contracts; do not extend the core receipt into a claim of item/event journaling.
Guilds/active recalls/social persistence, full ancillary synchronization, skills/buffs/quests/combat and original gameplay parity.
Original-client execution/build identification, non-ASCII/historical credential/timezone imports and performance acceptance.
Legacy packaged SQL Server drivers remain for unported paths; native tested runtime uses PostgreSQL only.
next_implementation: Close and durably drain native client sessions when the World peer connection is lost, gate admission on a registered replacement peer, and verify World restart/connection interruption before adding secondary Map transfer ownership.
